question: Air transport was launched in India in the year 1911 between which two places?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Allahabad and Naini**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On February 18, 1911, the first commercial civil aviation flight took place between Allahabad and Naini Junction, a distance of six miles, when Henri Piquet carried 6,500 pieces of mail on a Humber biplane.
 
• It quickly grabbed the spot of a “world first” in the process, as it is considered to be the world's first airmail service.
 
• The next year, in December, Indian State Air Services, along with Imperial Airways of the U.K., began a London-Karachi-Delhi flight, it becoming the first international flight to and from India.
 
• Between 1915 and 1929, there was a flurry of activity Tata Sons Ltd. (1915), and the Royal Air Force (1920) started regular air mail services between Karachi and Madras and Karachi and Bombay, and airports were constructed (1924) at Calcutta, Allahabad and at Bombay.
 
• Around this time the Department of Civil Aviation and the Aero Club of India also came into being (1927).
 
• The Indian Aviation Act was finalized in 1937, and Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) was set up with the help of the then Mysore Government in 1940.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Air India**

 
 
• Air India was established in the year 1932 by Tata Sons and was named Tata Air Services.
 
• Tata Air Services became a public sector company in the year 1946 and the name was changed to Air India.
 
• In 1953 under the Air Corporations Act, the government of India took control of Air India
